key_insight: PS2-RL learns a backup policy that implicitly defines a safe set online, then uses a differentiable projection layer to train RL policies with formal safety guarantees.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical way to add provable safety to existing RL pipelines without explicit invariant-set computation, making it more scalable for higher-dimensional control problems.
method: Phase 1: train a backup policy using a safe-arrival value function to construct an implicit control-invariant set.
Phase 2: train the RL policy end-to-end through a differentiable projection layer that enforces the learned safety constraints.
Maximize the implicit safe-set volume to reduce conservatism while preserving provable safety.
evidence_signal: The authors report theoretical guarantees and evaluate the method on robotic control tasks with state dimensions up to 10, where prior provably safe RL methods are often impractical.
watch_item: Safety depends on the quality of the learned backup policy and its implicit safe set, so imperfect backup training could limit guarantees or performance.
paper_title: Provably Safe, Yet Scalable Reinforcement Learning
